newsitem.title: BOSNIA: World Bank to set up private corp in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to set up private corp in Bosnia.

text.p: The World Bank said on Wednesday it plans to set up a private finance corporation in Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation to channel foreign funds and extend loans to local companies.

The World Bank will launch the corporation with some 50 million German marks ($28.9 million) collected from repayments of credit lines in the federation, said Rory O'Sullivan, director of the World Bank in Bosnia.

"We are getting close to 100 percent repayment rates on our credits to enterprises and industry and the idea is to feed this money back into the federation finance corporation," O'Sullivan told Reuters in an interview.

The corporation will be run privately by foreign and local banks, he said. Some foreign banks have already expressed interest in buying equity in the corporation, said O'Sullivan, who declined to name them.
"You'd probably get a really dynamic, forward looking foreign bank that understands the environment here and realises that this is something really for the future," he said.
The corporation would provide a significant boost for Bosnia's economic revival after a devastating 3-1/2 year war and would help lay the foundation for building a healthy banking system, he said.

Loans in Bosnia's peacetime economy are funded by World Bank and foreign donors' money and delivered through local banks. The system has been functioning with an extremely high return rate but it was always meant to be temporary, he said.

"We are getting out of the emergency methods of operation and into more normal business-like practices and the best way to do this is to bring in the private sector to apply the best kind of banking principles in giving loans to industry," he said.
"It's also isolated from political interest," he said.
The project is still in the planning phase and the finance corporation's precise structure has yet to be defined. But the World Bank hopes the corporation could be set up by the end of July.
O'Sullivan said the corporation would operate under rules which would benefit Bosnian businesses as well as the foreign banks who participate.
"The purpose of the whole thing is to improve the situation in Bosnia. It has to be a win-win situation for investor but very much for Bosnia as well," O'Sullivan said.
"We don't want to set up something that is just a money machine for foreign companies." ($ = 1.731 German Marks)
